name: Orbit AI - Phase 1 - Stripe payment to CRM

nodes.name: Stripe webhook
nodes.notes: NEW (brief v2): 'built now in Phase 1 with placeholder credentials, not deferred to Phase 5. Only Telnyx stays deferred.' options.rawBody:true is REQUIRED for the signature check in the next node to work at all - Stripe signs the exact raw request bytes, and if this node re-serializes the parsed JSON body instead of preserving the raw string, every signature check will fail even with a correct webhook secret. UNVERIFIED: whether 'rawBody' is the exact option name/nesting for the installed n8n version, and which expression exposes the raw string afterward ($json.body as a raw string vs $binary.data) - this is the single most likely thing in this entire workflow library to need hand-fixing on import. If it doesn't work as written, the safer fix is architectural, not a tweak: move signature verification into a tiny dedicated serverless function (Netlify Function or Cloudflare Worker, consistent with this repo's 'standalone service, not n8n Code nodes' principle for anything non-trivial) that verifies the signature with Stripe's own SDK and forwards only verified events to this webhook.

nodes.name: Verify signature & classify event
nodes.notes: Implements Stripe's documented signature scheme (t=timestamp,v1=hexHMAC over `${t}.${rawBody}` with the webhook secret) - the algorithm itself is stable public Stripe documentation, but this hasn't been tested against a real Stripe webhook delivery, and depends entirely on the previous node's raw-body assumption holding. ALSO ASSUMES the Checkout Session (or PaymentIntent) was created with metadata.opportunityId set to the Twenty CRM Opportunity ID - portal/netlify/functions/create-checkout-session.mts sets this already. Tier is reverse-derived from the paid amount against the brief's own known tier prices (Gold/Platinum/Iridium) - 'Unknown' for anything that doesn't match exactly (e.g. Rhodium's custom pricing), which downstream nodes should treat as a signal to flag for human review, not silently proceed as if it were a known tier. isFailure/failureReason are new this pass - a failed/expired payment now routes to a distinct dunning path (see 'Payment succeeded?' below) instead of being silently ignored as an 'irrelevant' event.

nodes.name: Payment succeeded?
nodes.notes: 06's audit-gap list: 'failed/declined payment handling - retry/dunning, distinct CRM state.' Splits the 'handled' (relevant) event stream in two - TRUE (isFailure is false, i.e. a real success) continues into the existing Won/Contract-creation path unchanged below; FALSE (a payment_intent.payment_failed or checkout.session.expired event) branches into a separate dunning path that writes a distinct Opportunity state and alerts a rep, instead of - as it would have before this pass - flowing straight into the Won-creation logic just because 'handled' was true for both.

nodes.name: Fetch Opportunity
nodes.notes: NEW (object model migration, CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md): reads the Opportunity's locationIds and companyName so the Company/Contract creation below has real data to work from, rather than guessing. This is where the funnel object (Opportunity) hands off to the client-relationship object (Company/Contract) - the single most structurally significant change in this pass.

nodes.name: Check Location Contract Lock

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ locationIds: ($json.data || $json).locationIds, opportunityId: $('Verify signature & classify event').item.json.opportunityId }) }}

nodes.notes: NEW this pass, real wiring (not just documented) - unlike DNC/compliant-hours' gates, whose caller is the not-yet-built live-dial engine, THIS gate's caller (this exact workflow) already exists in this repo, so there's no reason to leave it unwired. companyId is deliberately omitted - this is the new-logo Stripe path, no existing Company to compare against, so location-contract-lock-check.workflow.json will only ever find an UNRELATED-company conflict here, never an Amendment candidate. neverError:true is required so a 409 response comes back as normal data to branch on, not a thrown node error routing to errorWorkflow - the whole point is to branch cleanly, not treat 'blocked' as an unexpected failure.

nodes.name: Respond: blocked by Location lock

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, handled: false, reason: 'Location Contract Lock conflict - routed to human review, no Contract created.', conflicts: $json.conflicts }) }}

nodes.notes: Responds 200/ok:true to STRIPE (the payment already succeeded - Stripe doesn't care about internal CRM conflicts and shouldn't retry this webhook), NOT the location-contract-lock-check's own 409 - that distinction matters, this is a different HTTP boundary. The actual alert ('Location Contract Lock conflict', 05 Section 11) already fired from inside location-contract-lock-check.workflow.json itself, so this node doesn't duplicate it - a human now has to resolve the conflict manually; nothing here retries or auto-resolves, per the automation risk boundary's billing/contract-stage human gate.

nodes.name: Create Company

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ name: ($('Fetch Opportunity').item.json.data || $('Fetch Opportunity').item.json).companyName, status: 'LiveClient', liveClientSince: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

nodes.notes: NEW-LOGO PATH ONLY, deliberately: always creates a fresh Company rather than searching for an existing one first. An existing Company adding a Location/changing tier is Contract Amendment Flow (05 Section 13, 06's new addition) - explicitly Step 2/3 work per the agreed sequencing, NOT built this pass. If this workflow ever fires for an existing client (shouldn't happen via the new-logo Stripe Checkout flow, but worth stating), it will incorrectly create a duplicate Company - flagged here rather than silently handled, since building real dedup logic without Contract Amendment Flow existing yet would be guessing at half a solution.

nodes.name: Create Contract

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ companyId: $('Create Company').item.json.id, locationIds: ($('Fetch Opportunity').item.json.data || $('Fetch Opportunity').item.json).locationIds, status: 'Active', totalValue: $('Verify signature & classify event').item.json.amountTotalCents, agreementValue: $('Verify signature & classify event').item.json.amountTotalCents, tier: $('Verify signature & classify event').item.json.tier, startedAt: new Date().toISOString() }) }}

nodes.notes: Mirrors the winning Opportunity's Location set, per 05 Section 7 ('all Locations on the Contract reach Won together') and CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md's Contract object. totalValue/agreementValue both set to the paid amount for now - the brief distinguishes the two concepts (contract value vs. what's actually been agreed/collected) without fully specifying how they'd differ in a single-payment M2M scenario; worth revisiting once a multi-payment or discounted-term scenario exists to actually differentiate them.

nodes.name: Split Locations
nodes.notes: Fans the Contract's locationIds array out into one item per Location, same node type/pattern already used in referral-trigger.workflow.json. This branch is fire-and-forget relative to the HTTP response below (see 'Update Location contractStatus' notes) - deliberately not merged back into the main response chain, to avoid a second uncertain Merge node in an already-complex workflow.

nodes.name: Update Location contractStatus
nodes.notes: ASSUMES month-to-month (ActiveM2M) rather than a fixed term (ActiveTerm) - Stripe Checkout Session data alone doesn't distinguish these without a real subscription/price-object lookup, which isn't built. Runs once per Location (via Split Locations above) and intentionally doesn't feed back into the main response chain - if this PATCH fails for one Location, the webhook still responds 200 to Stripe (correct - Stripe doesn't care about internal CRM consistency) but the failure needs to surface via this workflow's errorWorkflow alert, not a failed HTTP response. This is exactly the Location Contract Lock field (CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md) - the enforcement workflow that actually BLOCKS a conflicting new Opportunity is Step 2/3, not built this pass; this node only makes sure the field gets set correctly so that enforcement has real data once it exists.

nodes.name: Create Billing Period

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ contractId: $('Create Contract').item.json.id, periodStart: new Date().toISOString(), periodEnd: new Date(Date.now() + 30*24*60*60*1000).toISOString(), revenueCents: $('Verify signature & classify event').item.json.amountTotalCents, commissionStatus: 'accrued' }) }}

nodes.notes: NEW (05 Section 15, Financial Tracking - new in v4): only the FIRST Billing/Accounting Period, created here so nothing downstream has to special-case 'no billing period yet exists' the moment a client goes live. The recurring MONTHLY generation for every subsequent period, the COGS breakdown (voice/STT/TTS/API costs - needs real per-client usage data this repo doesn't have anywhere yet), and commission calculation/approval are all Step 2/3 work, not built this pass. periodEnd is a naive +30 days, not calendar-month-aware - a real implementation should probably use actual month boundaries; flagged as a simplification, not a considered decision.

nodes.name: Advance Opportunity to Won

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ stage: 'Won', paymentStatus: 'Paid', onboardingProvisioningStatus: 'Pending', companyId: $('Create Company').item.json.id, contractId: $('Create Contract').item.json.id }) }}

nodes.notes: RENAMED from 'Live Client' to 'Won', matching 05 Section 7's own literal wording ('all Locations on the Contract reach Won together') - 'Live Client' was this workflow's own earlier invention before the object model existed; the ongoing-client status now belongs on the Company (set 'LiveClient' by the Create Company node above), not the Opportunity, per CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md's load-bearing pre-sale/post-sale distinction. onboardingProvisioningStatus:'Pending' kept from the previous version - W6.3's onboarding provisioning automation is still documented-only, not built. Same Twenty CRM REST-shape uncertainty as every workflow here.

nodes.name: Track opening-line outcome

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ opportunityId: $('Verify signature & classify event').item.json.opportunityId, openingLineId: ($('Fetch Opportunity').item.json.data || $('Fetch Opportunity').item.json).openingLineId, outcome: 'Won' }) }}

nodes.notes: Fire-and-forget, feeding opening-line-tracking.workflow.json (W4.7) - a safe no-op today since nothing writes openingLineId yet (Deep Dive Research isn't built). Reuses the Opportunity already fetched earlier in this workflow rather than a second GET.

nodes.name: Fetch Opportunity (dunning)
nodes.notes: Separate GET from the success path's 'Fetch Opportunity' (different branch entirely, no shared execution) - needed to read the current dunningAttemptCount so 'Write dunning state' can increment it rather than overwrite it, and companyName for the alert message.

nodes.name: Write dunning state

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ paymentStatus: 'Failed', dunningAttemptCount: (($('Fetch Opportunity (dunning)').item.json.data || $('Fetch Opportunity (dunning)').item.json).dunningAttemptCount || 0) + 1, lastPaymentFailureReason: $('Verify signature & classify event').item.json.failureReason }) }}

nodes.notes: New fields this pass, CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md's Opportunity object: paymentStatus:'Failed' is a distinct state from the 'Paid' the success path writes (06's exact framing: 'distinct CRM state'), dunningAttemptCount increments on every failed/expired event so a rep can see this isn't the first attempt, lastPaymentFailureReason carries Stripe's own last_payment_error.message through for context. No automatic retry is triggered here - retrying a charge is a billing action, gated to a human per the automation risk boundary, same as every other billing/contract-stage decision in this repo.

nodes.name: Alert: payment failed

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ severity: 'warning', source: 'stripe-payment-dunning', message: (($('Fetch Opportunity (dunning)').item.json.data || $('Fetch Opportunity (dunning)').item.json).companyName || 'Unknown company') + ' - payment failed (' + $('Verify signature & classify event').item.json.eventType + '): ' + ($('Verify signature & classify event').item.json.failureReason || 'no reason given') + '. Attempt #' + ((($('Fetch Opportunity (dunning)').item.json.data || $('Fetch Opportunity (dunning)').item.json).dunningAttemptCount || 0) + 1) + '.', linkUrl: ($env.TWENTY_CRM_BASE_URL || '') + '/objects/opportunity/' + $('Verify signature & classify event').item.json.opportunityId }) }}

nodes.notes: Routes to #portal-conversion (alertRouting.ts substring-matches 'stripe-payment' in the source string, and 'stripe-payment-dunning' contains it). severity:'warning', not 'critical' - a single failed payment isn't yet an emergency, a human just needs to see it and decide whether to follow up or retry the charge manually in Stripe. Recomputes the attempt count from 'Fetch Opportunity (dunning)' the same way 'Write dunning state' did, rather than trusting the PATCH response to echo the updated record back - that shape isn't verified for this Twenty CRM assumption, so this node doesn't depend on it.

nodes.name: Respond: handled (dunning)

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, handled: true, isFailure: true }) }}

nodes.notes: Responds 200 to Stripe same as the success path - the webhook was received and processed correctly either way; a failed payment isn't a webhook-delivery error, it's a business event this workflow now handles on its own distinct path.

nodes.name: Respond: ignored (valid, not relevant)
nodes.notes: Returns 200 for a validly-signed event this workflow doesn't act on, per Stripe's own guidance - responding with an error status to an event you're just not handling causes Stripe to retry it unnecessarily.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: false, reason: 'Invalid Stripe signature.' }) }}
